subject: FY2025 CDBG Action Plan
overview: The committee met to review the proposed $1.38 million Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Action Plan for fiscal year 2025. Representatives from various non-profit organizations and city departments presented funding requests for public services including elder care, transportation, food security, and housing assistance.

items.title: CDBG Allocation Overview
items.summary: CDBG Manager Laurel announced that the HUD allocation for fiscal year 2025 is $1,384,050, which is a 2.8% reduction from the current year but higher than original estimates.

items.title: Educational and Youth Services
items.summary: Megan Fidler-Carey requested $10,000 for Medford Public Schools afterschool scholarships, and Sarah Lodgen requested funding for The Welcome Project’s 'English for Parents' program.

items.title: Senior and Health Services
items.summary: Representatives from Community Family and the Council on Aging requested funds for dementia care scholarships, home maintenance for seniors, and social work outreach; Laurel also summarized a request for West Medford Community Center elder programming.

items.title: Transportation Services
items.summary: Nima of McGinn Transport and John Keegan of SCM Community Transportation described medical and grocery transit programs for seniors and residents with disabilities.

items.title: Food Security and Housing Assistance
items.summary: Applicants from Mystic Community Market, ABCD, and Housing Families presented requests for food distribution, mobile homeless outreach, and legal services to prevent eviction.

items.title: Referral of Action Plan
items.summary: Reported the paper out of committee favorably to the regular City Council meeting.
